audit_findings.title: Attributable numerator is divided by an all-unit denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 164.389m valuation shares versus 62.665m filed 2025 diluted Class A shares, a 2.62x denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: The numerator, consolidated add-backs, bridge assets and denominator represent different ownership claims, directly affecting OE and value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company uses the “if-converted method” to determine the potential dilutive effect of an assumed exchange of outstanding Common Units (and the cancellation of a corresponding number of shares of outstanding Class C Common Stock) for shares of Class A Common Stock and includes the dilutive effect of unvested Class A common shares in the diluted weighted average outstanding shares calculation.
audit_findings.explanation: The all-unit denominator is demonstrated, while the supplied record indicates a Class A-attributable or mixed numerator. Dividing a parent-attributable flow by all economic units understates value per Class A share, but consolidated add-backs or assets can offset or reverse that effect. The 2.62x denominator difference is large enough to change the conclusion, although the net error cannot be quantified without the OE component ledger.
audit_findings.action: Map every OE and bridge component to Class A or consolidated partnership claims, then rerun either a fully consolidated all-unit valuation or a fully parent-attributable Class A valuation.

audit_findings.title: Expansion capital may have been treated as perpetual maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed 2025 capital-spending pool was $529.671m versus a negative $333.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any expansion capital deducted as maintenance reduces anchor OE and causes a one-time growth investment to be capitalized as a recurring operating outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: Nearly 70% of the estimated capital expenditure is to be spent on continue expansion into the state of New Mexico to capitalize on expansive gathering system and early mover advantage, including the completion of the ECCC Pipeline, Phase 1 of the Kings Landing AGI project and the continued build out of the low and high pressure gathering system in the Eddy County, New Mexico.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes substantial expansion activity and total 2025 PP&E and intangible spending of $529.671m. It does not provide the 2025 maintenance-versus-growth split; the nearly 70% expansion disclosure applies to estimated 2026 spending. The error therefore remains a possibility rather than a demonstrated dollar adjustment, but the spending pool exceeds the absolute anchor and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $529.671m of 2025 spending project by project, classify sustaining and replacement capital separately from ECCC, Kings Landing, gathering-system expansion and acquisition-related spending, and rerun OE using only normalized maintenance capital.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be bridged at accounting cost or counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $1,987.074m carrying amount; valuation or double-count adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The stakes enter the equity bridge as a separate asset, while affiliate income, distributions or contributions may also remain in operating OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Under this method, the equity investments are carried originally at acquisition cost, increased by the Company’s proportionate share of the equity interest’s net income and contributions made, and decreased by the Company’s proportionate share of the equity interest’s net losses and distributions received.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1.9871bn bridge amount matches the June 2026 filed carrying values of PHP and Breviloba, demonstrating that the bridge uses accounting carrying amount rather than an independent economic valuation. Whether that amount overstates or understates fair value is unresolved, and the record does not prove whether affiliate economics were fully removed from OE. Because this bridge converts operating values of negative $3.551bn to negative $5.236bn into equity values of negative $1.556bn to negative $3.241bn, either misvaluation or double counting is material.
audit_findings.action: Independently value PHP and Breviloba net of venture-level liabilities and required capital, trace all equity income, distributions, contributions and basis amortization through OE, and rerun the bridge with no duplicated affiliate cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The negative anchor reverses the economic meaning of the scenarios
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $10.24 per share inversion between BEAR at negative $9.47 and BULL at negative $19.71; operating-PV difference $1.685bn
audit_findings.mechanism: Positive percentage growth applied to negative OE compounds losses, making higher-growth cases less valuable and carrying a negative anchor into the terminal-value formula.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the Company’s current financial plan, the Company believes that cash from operations and distributions from the EMI Pipelines and remaining borrowing capacity on our credit facilities will generate cash flows in excess of capital expenditures and the amount required to fund the Company’s planned quarterly dividend over the next 12 months.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling error: the stated BULL case is $10.24 per share below BEAR because 5% growth enlarges negative OE, while negative 2% growth shrinks it. Management's liquidity statement does not establish normalized OE, but it reinforces that an explicit recovery path must be tested. The current scenario labels and terminal mechanics cannot support the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace percentage-growth scenarios with explicit annual dollar paths for loss reduction, normalized operating cash flow and maintenance capital; permit terminal value only after OE becomes sustainably positive, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A booked environmental claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $14.0m, equal to approximately $0.09 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid environmental liability not captured in projected OE should be deducted from the equity bridge; the 2025 estimate reduction may also have increased anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The estimated environmental matter-related liability was $ 14.0 million and $ 24.0 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing confirms that the $14.0m liability remains outstanding and is expected to settle within twelve months. Assuming the entire amount is absent from OE and the bridge, deducting it would reduce value by about $0.09 per share. That is approximately 0.9% of the least-negative scenario equity deficit of $1.556bn and 0.16% of the computed $8.948bn market capitalization, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the settlement amount and whether the $14.0m is already captured in OE; deduct any uncaptured balance in the bridge, without treating it as a conclusion-changing item.

audit_findings.title: Long-term contract litigation may create an unreserved recurring burden
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed litigation costs were $16.988m for the six months ended June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Damages would reduce the equity bridge or OE, while specific performance or adverse contract-duration relief could impose recurring costs that reduce normalized OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company and certain of its affiliates are currently defending against two lawsuits brought by Energy Transfer GC NGL Product Services, LLC (formerly Lone Star NGL Product Services, LLC) individually and on behalf of certain of its affiliates, which allege breach of contract and related tort claims arising from two long-term NGL purchase agreements, and which seek remedies in the form of monetary damages, declaratory relief, and specific performance.
audit_findings.explanation: The stale trial-date concern is resolved factually: the latest 10-Q says a bench trial occurred in March and April 2026, the decision remains pending, and another trial concerning contract expiration is scheduled for October 2026. Immaterial reserves do not cap exposure, but no damages demand, pricing burden or probability-weighted loss is supplied. The finding may affect value materially, yet the current record cannot establish its magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the court rulings, October 2026 trial outcome, claimed damages and disputed contract terms; quantify any settlement, specific-performance pricing differential and remaining contract duration, then rerun OE and the bridge for costs not already recognized.
